title: Cotangent complexes and deformations in ringed topoi
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: The homotopical algebra in a ringed topos and the cohomology of diagrams on which the cotangent complex of a morphism of ringed topoi and its deformation theory rest. Homotopy sheaves of simplicial sheaves and the free abelian Whitehead theorem, with and without enough points; derived functors of non-additive functors of complexes in a ringed topos (cross-effects and degree, the Dold-Puppe bound, Deligne's homotopy invariance, the Deligne-Lazard theorem, a uniform bound for the derived functor); Koszul complexes and the shift formulas for symmetric, exterior and divided powers, with their products; décalage of simplicial objects, nerves of internal categories, groupoids and monoid actions, and Quillen's comparison of the homotopy theories of categories and simplicial sets; strict simplicial objects, the homology of the categories of simplices of strict simplicial sets, and Deligne's theorem that the categories of large finite ordinals and injective maps are contractible; derived colimits over a small category and over the category of finite ordinals and injective maps; fibred topoi, their total topoi, morphisms, direct images, and modules on total topoi; the cohomology of total topoi: standard resolutions, the cosimplicial complex computing derived direct images and derived limits, and direct images over a fixed index category; simplicial topoi, the décalage of a simplicial topos, the formula Rp_*p^*E = RHom(Z(X), E) for a simplicial object X of a topos, and cohomological descent for hypercoverings; the cohomology of the second total topos through the simplicial topos of a fibred topos, local systems, and a base change criterion; the left adjoints u_! of inverse images of modules on total topoi, their left derived functors and the adjunction RHom(Lu_!E, F) = RHom(E, u^*F), with derived colimits as a special case; local inductive limits as left adjoints, the left adjoints on the second total topos and their derived functors, derived colimits of simplicial modules, and the décalage statements for left adjoints; a duality formula for diagrams in a topos, which computes the Ext groups of a module of the first total topos into a module pulled back from the topos by the cohomology of the second total topos; equivariant sheaves on simplicial topoi: pseudo-categories, the category BX of equivariant sheaves with its two nerves, and coinduced and induced sheaves; the nerves of coinduced and induced modules as derived direct images and left adjoints along the décalages; the comparison of the cohomology and the derived Hom complexes of equivariant modules with those of the total topoi, with group cohomology as an example; the mixed Hom functor from the second total topos to the first, its compatibility with inverse images and derived left adjoints, and the computation of the Ext groups of equivariant modules by cosimplicial Hom groups, with Ext over a group ring and over a quiver as examples; multisimplicial objects and spectral diagrams, spectra of commutative group objects and the derived categories of spectral diagrams; the suspension theorem of Dold and Puppe and the stabilization of non-additive functors; stable derived functors as exact functors, with the free abelian group functor, whose stable homology is the module in degree 0 and vanishes in degree 1, and the symmetric, exterior and divided powers as examples. Simplicial rings and modules in a topos: homotopies, fibrations, cones and paths, and the calculus of fractions for quasi-isomorphisms; the suspension and loop functors, Ext groups, distinguished triangles and their long exact sequences, and the first Ext group described by extensions. Derived tensor products of simplicial modules and of simplicial algebras, and the derived extension of scalars, under which a quasi-isomorphism of simplicial rings induces an equivalence of derived categories. Spectral sequences for the homology of derived tensor products: from Tor groups degree by degree, the Künneth spectral sequence over the homology ring, and the Postnikov spectral sequence. Differential graded modules over a differential graded ring of a topos: truncations, bounded derived categories and truncated rings for rings in nonpositive degrees, derived Hom, derived tensor products and extension of scalars with their bounds, and the comparison of the derived tensor products of simplicial modules with those of their normalized complexes. Graded monoids and their actions over a monoidal category of indices: the simplicial categories C_•(J), graded objects as equivariant sheaves, the nerves of graded actions and the pseudo-category attached to them. Graded rings and modules: external tensor products of multisimplicial objects, induced modules over rings of type C_•(J), the equivalence between large simplicial rings and reduced spectral rings, and the description of modules over a ring by the spectra of the ring and the module. Diagonal rings: derived categories of modules over rings of type C_•(S_0) and over reduced rings of type C_•(S_1), the constant functor and its left adjoint through derived colimits over the nerve of the injective ordinals, and the comparison of derived Hom with derived Hom over the normalized double diagonal. The stable ring Z^st(A) of a ring: its ring structure through the spectrum of A, the augmentation, the computation of the derived tensor product of two rings through it, Mac Lane's theorem on A ⊗^L over Z^st(A) of Z^st(M), bar resolutions and the Mac Lane resolution of a module by sums of direct summands of the free modules on the products A^p × M^q. Ext groups of modules as cohomology of the nerve of the action of the spectrum of a ring on the spectrum of a module, with coefficients in the derived tensor product A ⊗^L O over a commutative ring O: a base change form of the comparison theorem for diagonal rings, the spectra of bounded complexes over A ⊗^L O, full faithfulness on two consecutive degrees, and relative cohomology along a homomorphism of modules. The Zariski and the big fppf sites of a scheme and of a diagram of schemes: quasi-coherent and adequate modules, bounded complexes with quasi-coherent cohomology and their truncated pullbacks, flat base change, and the equivalence for complexes of perfect amplitude in [a, b]. Deformations of diagrams of schemes: the cotangent complex of a morphism of diagrams, the classification of extensions by its first Ext group, deformations with cartesian ideal and the cartesian squares they preserve, and the obstruction to lifting a morphism over a thickened target as the product of the Kodaira-Spencer class with the class of the thickening. Equivariant cotangent complexes: category schemes acting on schemes and the classifying categories of their action categories, Tor independence, the equivariant cotangent complex as a projective system of truncations descended from the nerves, its Ext groups, pullbacks, the equivariant Kodaira-Spencer class and the change of the category scheme. Equivariant extensions and deformations: the conormal complex of a closed immersion into a smooth G-scheme, equivariant extensions and their classification by the equivariant cotangent complex, equivariant deformations of morphisms with the obstruction as a product with the equivariant Kodaira-Spencer class, the spectral sequence of the obstruction over the nerve, and morphisms between given equivariant extensions. Flat group schemes locally of finite presentation are local complete intersections: Frobenius kernels, the reduction over a field by quotients by Frobenius kernels, the fibre criterion over a base, and the cotangent complex at the unit. Torsors, co-Lie complexes and the Atiyah class: torsors under flat group schemes and their nerves as Cech nerves, descent of equivariant modules and of bounded complexes along a torsor on big fppf and Zariski sites, the co-Lie complex of a torsor, perfect with tor amplitude in [-1,0], its base change, the Atiyah triangle and the Atiyah class, their relation with the equivariant cotangent complex, and for smooth groups the coadjoint twist of the co-Lie module and the Atiyah exact sequence. Deformations of torsors: deformations of a torsor over a first-order thickening of the base are torsors and are the equivariant deformations of the projection; they are classified by Ext groups of the co-Lie complex, with the obstruction the product of the class of the thickening and the Atiyah class; duality, affine bases and smooth groups. The co-Lie complex of a group scheme: its perfect amplitude, its interpretation through torsors, functoriality, base change, the smoothness criterion, and the distinguished triangle of an exact sequence of group schemes, with roots of unity and Frobenius kernels as examples. The adjoint co-Lie complex: descent along torsors over diagrams of schemes, the co-Lie complex of the universal torsor over the nerve of a group scheme as an object of the classifying topos, the coadjoint action on invariant forms, and the distinguished triangle for the cotangent complex of the nerve, which expresses its Ext groups as relative Ext groups computed by a spectral sequence. Deformations of flat group schemes and of homomorphisms: deformations of a group law are deformations of its nerve; the obstruction, classification and automorphisms in Ext groups of the cotangent complex of the nerve, the product formula with the Kodaira-Spencer class, rigidity of etale groups, Hochschild cochains for smooth affine groups, and the extension and deformation of homomorphisms. Lie complexes of commutative group schemes: group schemes over diagrams and the shear isomorphism, additivity of the co-Lie complex, the co-Lie complexes of torsors under a commutative group and the triviality of the adjoint co-Lie complex, and the Lie complexes of the nerve and of the spectrum of a commutative group scheme. Lie complexes of module schemes: the spectral nerve of a module scheme as a commutative group scheme over that of the ring, the Lie complex with coefficients in the derived tensor product of the ring scheme and the structure ring, its tensor products, change of rings and exact sequences, and the Ext formula expressing the Ext groups of the cotangent complex of the spectral nerve as Ext groups of modules. Deformations of module schemes: deformations of a module scheme over a ring scheme are deformations of its spectral nerve; the obstruction, classification and automorphisms in Ext groups of modules into the Lie complex, the extension of homomorphisms and the deformation of a homomorphism with a given target, with etale module schemes and vector groups as examples. Graded modules and the graded cotangent complex: graded rings and modules in a topos, the adjoints of the degree functors, derived categories of graded modules, graded standard resolutions, the graded cotangent complex with its comparison with the cotangent complex and its parts in degrees zero and one, the graded transitivity triangle, graded square-zero extensions and the first truncation. The Atiyah class of a module: principal parts over the standard resolution, the Atiyah class and its naturality, its description through the graded cotangent complex of the dual numbers, the principal parts extension and connections. Deformations of modules and of their morphisms: extensions of modules over a square-zero thickening, the canonical class from the derived tensor product, the obstruction, classification and automorphisms, the canonical class as the product of the Atiyah class and the class of the thickening, the universal thickening, connections and unobstructedness, and the extension and deformation of morphisms. Filtered derived categories: complexes with finite filtrations, filtered quasi-isomorphisms, the filtered and graded derived categories, truncation and filtration intervals, filtered objects and their Yoneda extensions, the filtered derived Hom and its spectral sequence with the signs of its first differential. Filtered tensor products on a ringed topos: graded pieces of tensor products, filtered K-flat and K-injective resolutions, the derived tensor product as a symmetric monoidal structure compatible with the associated graded, derived pullback, finite tor dimension. Filtered internal Hom and the formulas of Cartan: the filtered derived Hom, global sections, Cartan's isomorphism, evaluation, composition and product morphisms, the adjunction between derived pullback and pushforward, global products. Perfect filtered complexes and duality: finiteness conditions, amplitude estimates, biduality and the product isomorphisms, and the characterization of the dualizable objects as the filtered perfect complexes. Traces and cup products of perfect filtered complexes: twisted traces in symmetric monoidal categories, additivity of traces for filtered morphisms, multiplicativity, cup products, invariance under conjugation and base change. Filtered and graded powers of complexes: the filtrations of symmetric, exterior and divided powers of a filtered module, their graded pieces for flat graded pieces, the Koszul filtration of a power of an extension, derived powers on the bounded above filtered and graded derived categories with their graded pieces, products and amplitude. Filtered Koszul complexes and the shift isomorphisms: filtered Koszul sequences, the shift isomorphisms on filtered and graded derived categories, their graded pieces with the signs, and their products. Diagonal maps of symmetric and exterior powers: the multiplicative maps from powers of a tensor product to tensor products of powers, their graded pieces, their compatibility with Koszul sequences and shift isomorphisms, for complexes concentrated in degrees at most zero. L-series of endomorphisms of perfect complexes: the rings of series of derived powers, with the shift isomorphisms as ring isomorphisms; the trace of a shifted morphism; the L-series and the characteristic series of a morphism E -> E (x) M with M concentrated in degrees at most zero, their naturality, invariance, base change, additivity on filtrations, multiplicativity on gradings and behaviour under shifts, the formula through exterior powers, and the characteristic series of a map of strictly perfect complexes as an alternating product of determinants. The Atiyah class of filtered complexes: the Atiyah class of complexes, written E -> E (x) L[1], natural and compatible with base change and with shifts without sign; normalization of filtered simplicial objects; filtered complexes with filtration in [0,n] as chains of modules on the total topos of the constant fibred topos over [n]; the filtered Atiyah class with graded pieces the classes of the graded pieces; the class of the principal parts of B over A. Chern classes of perfect complexes: total Chern classes with values in the exterior powers of the cotangent complex, multiplicative on filtrations, gradings and distinguished triangles, with base change, the rank bound, and Chern classes in Hodge cohomology, including the first Chern class of an invertible module through the extension of principal parts. Chern classes with supports from partial connections: the topos Top^o(i) of an open subset and its complement, whose cohomology with coefficients (0 -> F) is cohomology with supports in the complement; principal parts of a derivation into a locally free module; partial connections as maps satisfying the Leibniz rule along a quotient of the differentials; the localized class on Top^o(i); Chern classes with supports lifting the Chern classes relative to the derivation, and Chern polynomials of weight larger than the rank of the kernel in cohomology with supports; Bott's partial connection on the normal module of an involutive submodule of the tangent module, with the vanishing of its Chern polynomials of high weight in Hodge cohomology when the submodule is a direct summand everywhere. Weakly regular ideals: strict graded commutativity of the homotopy of simplicial rings; the Tor algebra of a quotient ring through simplicial resolutions, the conormal isomorphism and the canonical map from the exterior algebra of the conormal module; the bigraded algebra Tor(B, gr_I A), on which the connecting maps are a derivation, and its homomorphism from the Koszul complex of the conormal module; for weakly regular ideals gr_I(A) is the symmetric algebra of I/I^2 and the Koszul complex resolves Tor(B, A/I^(n+1)); the ideal of the variables of the symmetric algebra of a flat module and Koszul-regular ideals are weakly regular. Connectivity of powers of simplicial ideals: connectivity of derived tensor products, detection of connectivity after base change to pi_0 of a simplicial ring, connectivity of the Koszul terms of a module with vanishing pi_0, and Quillen's convergence theorem: the powers J^m of a degreewise weakly regular simplicial ideal with pi_0(J) = 0 are m-connective, so the filtration of Tor by the powers of the augmentation ideal of the standard resolution is finite in each degree. The fundamental spectral sequence: the augmentation ideal J of the Tor resolution has J/J^2 = L_{B/A} and J^q/J^(q+1) = S^q(L_{B/A}); products of classes of degree one give Lambda^q(pi_1 L) = pi_q(S^q L) for 1-connective L, with a comparison of S^q L and S^q(pi_1(L)[1]) in a range of degrees; spectral sequences of multiplicatively filtered differential graded rings; the fundamental spectral sequence H(S^q L_{B/A}) => Tor^A(B, B), its convergence and its edge homomorphism; for B = A/I, I is weakly regular if and only if the André-Quillen homology D_q(B/A, M) vanishes for q >= 2, if and only if I/I^2 is flat and L_{B/A} = (I/I^2)[1]; Koszul-regular quotients. Weak complete intersections: tor amplitude in a ringed topos (connectivity, triangles, base change, faithfully flat descent); homomorphisms whose cotangent complex has tor amplitude in [-1, 0], with polynomial algebras, quotients by weakly regular ideals and local complete intersections as examples; stability under composition, cancellation and faithfully flat descent; for a quotient of an algebra with flat differentials, weak complete intersection if and only if the kernel is weakly regular, with the two-term model I/I^2 -> Omega (x) B; Tor-independent base change in topoi with enough points and for schemes. Weakly regular ideals of noetherian rings: the exact sequence H_3(L) -> Lambda^2(I/I^2) -> Tor_2(B, B) -> H_2(L) -> 0; the sequence linking Koszul homology H_1(f; A) with Tor_2; the Ext criterion for weakly regular ideals with projective conormal module; over a noetherian local ring, generation by a regular sequence iff D_2(B/A, k) = 0; over a noetherian ring, equivalence of weak regularity, regular and Koszul-regular ideals, S(I/I^2) = gr_I(A), and the vanishing of D_2 or Ext^2 for finite modules; for algebras of finite type over a noetherian ring, local complete intersections are the weak complete intersections; morphisms of schemes locally of finite type over a locally noetherian base, and regular immersions. Regular local rings and complete intersections: D_1(k/A) is the embedding dimension; A is regular iff D_2(k/A) = 0 iff L_{k/A} = (m/m^2)[1]; the cotangent complex of the residue field does not change under completion; power series over fields and Cohen rings are regular; for a presentation by a regular local ring, D_q(k/A) = D_{q-1}(-/P, k) for q >= 3 and the four-term sequence in degree two; A is a complete intersection iff D_3(k/A) = 0 iff D_q(k/A) = 0 for q >= 3, the kernel of every presentation then being generated by a regular sequence; minimal presentations and dim D_2(k/A) as the number of relations. The arrow topos and relative Ext groups: the arrow topos XY of a morphism of ringed topoi f: X -> Y, with its restrictions to X and Y and its projection to Y; RGamma(XY, (E <- F)) = RGamma(Y, F); derived Hom out of objects over X, out of quasi-cartesian objects and out of objects over Y, with trivial duality; the relative Ext groups Ext^i(Y/X; M, F) and their long exact sequence with Ext^i(M, F) and Ext^i(Lf^*M, Lf^*F) (for an open subspace, cohomology with supports in the closed complement); the category of triples (E, F, Lf^*F -> E) of the derived categories is not triangulated, and the comparison of Hom groups with D(XY) is surjective with kernel the image of Ext^{-1}; the cotangent complex of the morphism of arrow topoi defined by a square of ringed topoi. Deforming a morphism together with its target: for a square-zero thickening Z of Z_o, morphisms f_o: X_o -> Y_o and flat g_o: Y_o -> Z_o, and a flat deformation X of X_o over Z, the flat deformations of Y_o over Z with an extension of f_o to X have an obstruction in Ext^2(Y_o/X_o; L_{Y_o/Z_o}, g_o^*K), form a torsor under Ext^1, and have as automorphisms the derivations of Y_o over Z_o into g_o^*K vanishing on X_o; the same for any coefficients (I <- J) in the arrow topos; the obstruction is the product of the Kodaira-Spencer class of X_oY_o -> X_oZ_o -> S with the class of the thickening; if Y_o deforms, the obstruction comes from Ext^1(Lf_o^*L_{Y_o/Z_o}, h_o^*K); locally ringed topoi, schemes and closed immersions are preserved. De Rham complexes and Lie algebroids: antiderivations of exterior algebras in a topos; a pair of first-order operators extends to an antiderivation; Omega^bullet_{A/K} is the initial de Rham complex; a quotient of Omega^1_{A/K} carries a de Rham complex exactly when d of its relations vanishes in the second exterior power (some quotients carry none); the Lie algebroid of a de Rham complex through Cartan's formulas and the Chevalley-Eilenberg formula; for locally free modules of finite type the Jacobi identity is equivalent to d^2 = 0 and de Rham complexes are anti-equivalent to Lie algebroids; invariant differential forms on a torsor under a flat group scheme form a de Rham complex, with the Lie algebra of left-invariant derivations and the Atiyah sequence, whose kernel is the Lie algebra of the group twisted by the torsor. Formal categories with divided powers and the Čech–Alexander complex: pro-algebras and formal categories (internal categories of the opposite of pro-algebras), their nerves and augmentation ideals; divided powers on sheaves of ideals; divided powers on the augmentation ideal of an augmented algebra extend along every base change, without flatness, so the nerve of an affine category with divided powers on its augmentation ideal carries them in every degree, compatibly with the cofaces exactly when the composition is a PD morphism; PD completions; divided power envelopes of tensor products of augmented algebras; the Čech–Alexander complex of A/K. The de Rham complex of a formal category with divided powers: the Alexander-Whitney algebra of a cosimplicial algebra and its normalized subalgebra; the tensor algebra of the augmentation ideal maps to the normalized nerve, isomorphically when the source and target maps agree on A; the module of differentials I/I^[2] and the exterior derivative, a complex when d^0 = d^1, when Omega^1 is generated by differentials of functions, or when it is flat; for the Čech–Alexander complex of A/K it is the de Rham complex of A/K. Décalage and the formal Poincaré lemma: the shifted category of a PD formal category, with de Rham complex P (x) Omega^bullet_R; when Omega^1 is flat, the graded ring of the divided power filtration of the arrows is the divided power algebra Gamma(Omega^1), the graded de Rham complex is the Koszul complex of the identity, and the augmented de Rham complex of the shifted category is acyclic modulo every step of the filtration (the formal Poincaré lemma); for polynomial algebras this is the divided power Poincaré lemma. Cohomology of flat formal categories with divided powers: for a PD-adic formal category with flat Omega^1, the graded nerve is Gamma of the Dold-Puppe nerve of Omega^1[-1], the tensor algebra of the augmentation ideal is the normalized cochain algebra, and the normalized cochains are quasi-isomorphic to the de Rham complex, compatibly with the divided power and Hodge filtrations; the rank one case is a contractible complex of cut points. Cotangent complexes of simplicial rings: the diagonal of the degreewise standard resolution; for degreewise symmetric algebras of flat modules it is computed by Kähler differentials; it is invariant under quasi-isomorphisms, it is the left derived functor of C -> Omega^1_{C/A} (x)_C B and it corepresents derivations in the homotopy category of algebras; every degreewise free resolution of a map of rings computes its cotangent complex. Localization morphisms and the cotangent complex: rings of fractions in a topos, localization morphisms and their stability; flat epimorphisms have vanishing cotangent complex; localization of ringed topoi; on affine schemes the cotangent complex is the module associated with that of the rings, with quasi-coherent (and in the noetherian finite type case coherent) homology; Tor-independent base change for rings of a topos and for ringed topoi whose structure rings are localizations of tensor products, as for fibre products of schemes. The derived de Rham complex: the realization of the de Rham complexes of a free resolution, with the Hodge filtration and graded pieces the derived exterior powers of the cotangent complex; independence of the free resolution; triviality over rings containing Q; the Hodge completion and its computation by Čech–Alexander complexes; derived exterior powers of two-term complexes as Koszul complexes of divided powers, and the graded pieces for weak complete intersections. Derived de Rham complexes in characteristic p: the Cartier map into the cohomology of the de Rham complex and the Cartier isomorphism for free algebras and smooth morphisms; the conjugate filtration and the derived Cartier isomorphism on its graded pieces; the derived de Rham complex of a smooth morphism is its de Rham complex, and that of a relatively perfect map is the algebra. The completed derived de Rham complex of a complete intersection: weakly smooth algebras; the first graded piece of the completed Čech nerve of a presentation is the two-term complex I/I^2 -> Omega^1 (x) B; over a ring containing Q the graded pieces are its symmetric powers, the completed Čech nerve does not depend on the presentation, and it is filtered quasi-isomorphic to the Hodge-completed derived de Rham complex. The simplicial derived category of a topos: mapping objects, homotopies and mapping cylinders of simplicial sheaves; for simplicial sets, quasi-isomorphisms through the Kan replacement, monomorphic quasi-isomorphisms into Kan complexes are anodyne, and pushouts along monomorphisms preserve quasi-isomorphisms; the homotopy category as the localization at homotopy equivalences, the simplicial derived category, and the calculus of left fractions when the topos has enough points, also over a fixed simplicial sheaf. Local fibrations and Kan's subdivision functor: strict anodyne extensions and their pushout products, the local lifting property and fibrations of simplicial sheaves (stability, inverse images, points); for simplicial sets, subdivision, the last vertex map, Kan's theorem that Ex^∞ X is a Kan complex quasi-isomorphic to X, Ex preserves Kan fibrations, a Kan fibration that is a quasi-isomorphism lifts against every monomorphism, and a monomorphism is anodyne exactly when it is a quasi-isomorphism; Ex^∞ of simplicial sheaves; base change of fibrant quasi-isomorphisms when the topos has enough points. Simplicial groups and right fractions: Moore's theorem for simplicial groups of a topos (homotopy sheaves are the homology of the normalized complex, also non-abelian), fibrations and fibrant quasi-isomorphisms of simplicial groups through the normalized complex; mapping objects relative to maps and their fibrations; path factorization; right fractions among Kan simplicial sheaves when the topos has enough points; the Kan derived category is the simplicial derived category in every topos, the homotopy category of Kan complexes for the topos of sets; the same over a simplicial sheaf B, with a functorial fibrant replacement over B. Hypercoverings and Ext groups of free simplicial modules: with enough points, the free simplicial module functor is left adjoint to the forgetful functor on simplicial derived categories; the Ext groups of free simplicial modules through the Hom complex of a simplicial sheaf and a simplicial module, and as colimits over fibrant quasi-isomorphisms; hypercoverings as the fibrant quasi-isomorphisms to the final object and Verdier's hypercovering theorem; for the classifying topos of Z, the homotopy category of Kan simplicial sheaves is not the simplicial derived category.
prerequisites: sites, sheaves, topoi and sheaves of modules (the Stacks project, chapters Sites and Sheaves and Modules on Sites)
derived categories and derived functors (the Stacks project, chapter Derived Categories)

simplicial sets, nerves and Kan complexes; test categories and Quillen's Theorem A (programme course Algebraic spaces and stacks, lessons Simplicial sets, nerves and Kan complexes and Test categories and Grothendieck's homotopy programme)

checks.reading: The choice of topics follows Illusie's work on the cotangent complex, which each lesson credits by name. The proofs were written for this course from the Stacks project (sites, modules, derived categories, simplicial methods), the programme's lessons on simplicial sets and test categories, and the free sources listed below. Several statements are proved by routes different from the classical ones: Deligne's contractibility theorem through a contraction of comma categories and Quillen's Theorem A, the homology of categories of simplices through a double complex, and the total topoi through explicit sites.

open_obligations: The Artin-Mazur criterion, which detects weak equivalences of simplicial sets and of categories through cohomology with local coefficients, is not proved; no lesson uses it.

For a good fibred topos whose left adjoints f_! do not preserve fibre products, the second total category is a topos by Giraud's theorem, which is not proved; the lessons use that category as a topos only under the hypothesis of Theorem 4.3 of the lesson on fibred topoi.

The canonical homotopy equivalence between a simplicial object of an additive category with coproducts and its simplicial replacement, its comparison with diagonals of multisimplicial objects, and the corresponding statement for functors on the truncated categories of injective ordinals, are not yet proved; for simplicial modules over a ring of a topos, a quasi-isomorphism between the two is proved (lesson on derived left adjoints on the second total topos, Lemma 4.1).
The comparison of the derived colimit over finite ordinals and injective maps with the termwise colimit is proved when the terms are colimit-acyclic; the general case is not settled.

For simplicial modules, the diagonal of the total décalage is expected to be quasi-isomorphic to the original object; this is not yet proved. Example 1.4 of the lesson on décalage shows that it is not a homotopy equivalence in general.

Diagrams of diagrams and their types are not treated. The adjunction of derived colimits is proved as an isomorphism of RHom complexes for diagrams of modules over a ring of a topos (lesson on left derived functors of left adjoints, Proposition 4.1); for diagrams in a general abelian category it is proved in its Ext form only.
The free abelian Whitehead theorem without hypotheses on points or additivity depends on Barr's theorem on Boolean localizations, which is not proved.
The compatibility of the standard resolutions of total topoi with morphisms of fibred topoi is not treated; the left derived functors of the left adjoints u_! of inverse images of modules need it.
The cohomology of the second total topos is treated when that category is a topos; for an arbitrary good fibred topos this depends on Giraud's theorem (see above).

The base change criterion for direct images on the second total topoi is proved under an additional condition (inverse images on the target carry injectives to totally acyclic sheaves, or finitely many strings of each length start at each object); the general case is not proved.
The formula for Lu_! by standard resolutions of non-flat complexes is proved when the module inverse images of the source are exact as well; without that condition it is not proved.

The left derived functors of the left adjoints u_! on the second total topoi are proved under a condition on the left adjoints f_! of the source (they preserve flat modules and short exact sequences of flat modules); without it they are not proved.

The category BX of equivariant sheaves on a pseudo-category is a topos by Giraud's theorem, which is not proved; the lessons use only that its modules form an abelian category with enough injectives, which is proved directly.

The identification of the nerves of induced modules with left adjoints along the décalage is proved for two-sided pseudo-categories, which include the nerves of internal categories; for other good pseudo-categories it is not proved.

The comparison of all derived Hom complexes of equivariant modules with those of the total topoi is proved under the exactness condition on left adjoints as well as the injectivity condition, and for the first total topos for two-sided pseudo-categories; under the injectivity condition alone it is proved for complexes of modules with invertible structure, which include the structure ring, so for the cohomology.

The compatibility of the mixed Hom functor with inverse images is proved for bounded above complexes, and its compatibility with derived left adjoints for bounded above complexes; the unbounded versions (along a morphism of finite Tor dimension, respectively under exactness of the left adjoints on all complexes) are not proved.
The internal mixed Hom and the duality formula are proved for diagrams in a topos; their versions for diagrams of diagrams are not treated.

The stable homology of the free abelian group functor is computed in degrees 0 and 1 (X and 0). Cartan's values in degrees 2 and 3 (X/2X and the 2-torsion of X) and the vanishing of the rational stable homology in positive degrees are stated with their source and not proved. The identification of this stabilization with Breen's stable Eilenberg-MacLane complex is not treated.

The isomorphisms between the stable derived functors of S^n, Lambda^n and Gamma^n are proved, naturally, for complexes concentrated in nonpositive degrees. Their naturality on all bounded above complexes needs a comparison with the shift isomorphism of the stabilization, which is not carried out.

That the functor from true triangles, short exact sequences of simplicial modules up to quasi-isomorphism, to distinguished triangles is in general not an equivalence is stated without proof; its essential surjectivity and conservativity are proved.

The Künneth spectral sequence for derived tensor products of simplicial modules is constructed as a spectral sequence of abelian sheaves whose first two pages are modules over the homology ring of the simplicial ring; that its higher differentials and the identification of its abutment are linear over the whole homology ring is stated and not proved.

The homomorphism from the Ext groups of the abelian category of simplicial modules to the Ext groups defined through the suspension, obtained from the diagonal of bisimplicial modules, is not treated; nor is the derived extension of scalars on true triangles.

The extension of the spectrum of complexes of modules to modules over A ⊗^L_Z O (lesson on Ext groups as cohomology of spectral nerves, Definition 3.2) is constructed on bounded complexes, and its compatibility with derived tensor products over O is proved when the result is bounded; the extension to bounded above and unbounded complexes, and the compatibility with derived tensor products for all bounded above complexes, are not proved.

That this extension is not fully faithful on all bounded complexes is expected, through the nonvanishing of the stable homology of the free abelian group functor in degree 2, but it is not proved; it depends on Cartan's values, which are stated and not proved (see above).

Illusie's comparison of the Zariski and the big fpqc topoi of a scheme (in a fixed universe) is treated with the big fppf site in place of the big fpqc site; the fpqc version, which needs a choice of universe, is not treated.

The equivariant transitivity triangle (lesson on equivariant cotangent complexes, Proposition 3.3) is constructed as maps between the truncations together with the long exact sequences of Ext groups; Illusie's form of it as a projective system of filtered objects, which needs filtered derived categories, is not constructed.

For a closed immersion into a smooth G-scheme, Illusie's isomorphisms of the truncated equivariant cotangent complex with the equivariant conormal complex are canonical; the lesson on equivariant extensions and deformations proves that isomorphisms with the stated compatibilities exist and shows that they are not unique in general (its Exercise 6.3); a canonical choice, through Illusie's construction for III 3.1.3, is not constructed.

The interpretation of the equivariant deformation obstruction in the spectral sequence of the nerve (Illusie VII 2.3.4.1 and 2.3.4.2 c), d): the identification of its filtration with restrictions to the truncated nerves, the obstruction to extending the action, and the associativity defect) is not proved; the edge map to the obstruction for the underlying morphism of schemes is proved.

Illusie's VII 2.3.5 b) (equivariant deformations of g given an equivariant deformation of h = gf, classified by relative Ext groups) is not proved; it needs relative Ext groups and the non-equivariant theorem III 2.3.

Illusie's true Atiyah triangle (VII 2.4.2.1) is an object of pro-D_F^{b[0,1]}, a projective system of filtered objects, and his descent statements (2.4.1.2) are also stated for pro-D_F^{b[a,b]}; the lesson on torsors constructs, for each truncation, the distinguished Atiyah triangle and its maps and proves descent for bounded complexes and their projective systems of truncations; the filtered forms, which need filtered derived categories, are not constructed.

Illusie's VII 2.4.5 a) is proved in The adjoint co-Lie complex of a group scheme (Section 1) for torsors under a group scheme over S over a diagram of schemes, the case used in VII 3.1.2; the version for group objects over the diagram (used in VII 4.1.2) and 2.4.5 b) (torsors over relative schemes over a ringed topos, in the sense of Hakim) are not treated.
The lessons were written and checked by one model in one session; they have not been checked by a second reader.

Illusie's definition VII (3.1.2.1) of the co-Lie complex with the adjoint action, as the descent of the equivariant cotangent complex of G x G^o acting on G by (g,h)x = gxh along the equivalence B(G x G^o)/G -> BG, and its identification (3.1.2.4) with the nerve form used in the course (The adjoint co-Lie complex of a group scheme, Proposition 2.2) are not treated; nor are the contravariance of the adjoint co-Lie complex in G, its compatibility with base change S' -> S (VII 3.1.2), and the interpretations (3.1.2.5)-(3.1.2.6) through the universal torsor PG over BG and the twisting formula for G^o_Y-torsors.

VII 3.1.3.2 in the form RHom(L eps^* L_{Ner(G)/S}, ner M) = RGamma(BG/S, ll_G^v (x)^L M)[1], with the dual of the adjoint co-Lie complex on the classifying topos, needs that complex to be perfect on BG and RHom(ll_G, M) = RGamma(BG, ll_G^v (x)^L M) (SGA 6 I 7.7 on BG); the course proves the equivalent relative Ext form (The adjoint co-Lie complex of a group scheme, Corollary 3.5), with the dual only in the E_1 terms of the spectral sequence. The same applies to the forms of VII 3.2.1 and 3.3.1 with H^q(BG/S, ll_G^v (x)^L e^*I) and H^q(BF/S, u^*ll_G^v (x)^L e^*I) (Deformations of flat group schemes and of homomorphisms, Theorems 2.1 and 3.1, in relative Ext form).

VII 3.2.2 b), c) and Remarks 3.3.1.1 b): the interpretation of the graded pieces of the spectral filtration of the obstructions (deforming the multiplication modulo choices, the Hochschild associativity cocycle, the multiplicativity defect of a lift and the classification of lifts up to inner automorphisms of SGA 3 III 2), and the identification of the edge map of the spectral sequence with restriction to the level 1; the course proves the restriction statement in nerve form (Deformations of flat group schemes and of homomorphisms, Proposition 2.2).

VII 3.3.2 in the relative cohomology form with the object K defined by the functoriality map of the Lie complexes (Remark 3.1.3.3 (ii)), and Remarks 3.3.2.1 b), d); the course proves 3.3.2 in nerve form (Deformations of flat group schemes and of homomorphisms, Theorem 3.3); the relative form needs the contravariance of the adjoint co-Lie complex.

VII 3.3.3 (deforming the target group scheme together with an extension of a homomorphism from a given deformed source), which rests on the relative deformation theory of III 2.3.2, and Remarks 3.3.3.1.

VII 4.1.1.1 and 4.1.1.2 (base change maps for classifying topoi: along a morphism of monoids acting on an object, and for the addition map of a commutative group), auxiliary to the proof of VII 4.1.1 after Deligne; the course proves VII 4.1.1 by the shear isomorphism instead (Lie complexes of commutative group schemes, Corollary 2.3).

VII 4.1.3 for a commutative group scheme over a diagram S, as stated by Illusie with the triangle (3.1.3.1) over diagrams; the course proves it for a scheme S (Lie complexes of commutative group schemes, Proposition 3.1), the triangle of The adjoint co-Lie complex of a group scheme, Theorem 3.3, being proved over a scheme.
VII (4.1.2.4) for M in D^+(Top^o(S_fpqc)) unbounded above; the course proves it for M in D^b (Lie complexes of commutative group schemes, Proposition 1.6), which covers its uses.

VII (4.1.5.1) for M in D^-(S_fpqc) unbounded below; the course proves it for M in D^b (Lie complexes of module schemes, Proposition 3.3), the functor Psi of Ext groups of modules as cohomology of spectral nerves being defined on bounded complexes; the uses in VII 4.1.6 and 4.2 have M in D^b.

VII 4.2.0 with Illusie's hypothesis that A itself is Tor independent of S and S' over T; Deformations of module schemes assumes it for all finite fibre powers A^P (which the levels of the spectral nerves need, and which holds when A is flat over T); whether Tor independence of A alone suffices is not settled.

VII 4.2.1 (iii) in the form omega(G,i) = e(i) c(A,G/S/T) with c in Ext^1_A(G, l^v_G (x)^L t_[ L eps^* L_{S/T}); the course proves the nerve form with the class of N(A,S') as a T-extension (Deformations of module schemes, Theorem 2.1 (3)); the factorization needs that class as a pullback of e(i) and the Ext formula with coefficients in L_{S/T}.

VII Remarks 4.2.2 a), b), 4.2.4 a), 4.2.6 b), c): the comparison of the obstructions with those for commutative group schemes (restriction to Ext_Z) and for group schemes through the map (4.2.2.1) RHom_Z(G,M) -> RGamma(BG/S,M)[1], and the compatibility of the obstructions of 4.2.5 with differences of deformations of G.

VII 4.2.7 and Remarks 4.2.8 (deforming the target A-module scheme together with an extension of a homomorphism from a given deformed source, Oort's lifting result under a vanishing hypothesis), which rest on the relative deformation theory of III 2.3.2, as VII 3.3.3.
VII 4.2.9: the comparison of the vector-group case with IV 3.1, III 3.2.3 and III 3.2.12; the course computes the vector-group case directly (Deformations of module schemes, Proposition 3.2).

IV 1.2.4, (2.2.6)-(2.2.7) and (2.3.1)'-(2.3.5)': graded simplicial rings, the diagonal graded cotangent complex with its corepresentation of graded derivations in the homotopy category of graded simplicial algebras, and the graded transitivity triangle for graded simplicial rings; they rest on the ungraded II 1.2.5-1.2.6.7 (plan lesson B1). With them the graded description of the Atiyah class of a simplicial module (IV 2.3.6 for simplicial M); Graded modules and the graded cotangent complex treats constant graded rings and The Atiyah class of a module defines the class of a simplicial module through principal parts.

IV Remark 2.3.7.5: comparison of the class of the Atiyah sequence of the frame torsor of a locally free module (Torsors, co-Lie complexes and the Atiyah class, Proposition 4.2) with the class of its principal parts extension, including the sign for the course's conventions (The Atiyah class of a module, Remark 3.5). Consumer: V (5.9.4), the image of the class of an invertible module in Pic under g -> g^{-1}dg as its first Chern class in Hodge cohomology; Chern classes of perfect complexes, Proposition 2.4, proves c'^1(E) = minus the class of the principal parts extension twisted by E^vee and nabla_{ge} = nabla_e - g^{-1}dg.

IV 3.1.12-3.1.13 in Illusie's form: the derivation of the exact sequence (3.1.4) from the graded transitivity triangle of B -> B_o -> B_o + M_o (which needs the coefficients I + J(-1), with M_o acting through u_o, and the graded obstruction theorem) and its comparison with the sequence of the derived tensor product; Deformations of modules and of their morphisms proves (3.1.4)-(3.1.5) through the derived tensor product.

IV 3.2.12-3.2.14 and Exercises 3.2.15-3.2.16 in Illusie's form: the single obstruction class in Ext^2_{B_o}(C(f_o),K) for deforming a morphism with given source, the identification of the solutions with a torsor under Ext^1_{B_o}(C(f_o),K), the case of quotient modules, and the canonical obstruction through the Atiyah class of f_o; Deformations of modules and of their morphisms, Proposition 4.2, proves the two-step criterion, the automorphisms and the structure of the set of solutions.

IV Exercise 3.1.14: for a closed immersion of smooth S-schemes Y -> X, the obstruction to deforming an invertible module to the first infinitesimal neighbourhood through the boundary of the conormal sequence and d log, and the Segre quadric P^1 x P^1 in P^3 over Z, where omega(i,L_1) = -omega(i,L_2) generates H^2(Y,N_{Y/X}) (Deformations of modules and of their morphisms, Exercise 5.3, proves the unobstructedness part).

V 2.3.4 (last paragraph): compatibility of the composition morphism with the product morphism of internal Homs (Filtered internal Hom and the formulas of Cartan, Definition 3.2), and the corresponding relation between the global composition and the global product (2.3.6.5).

V 3.8 (after 3.8.7): the internal commutative diagram expressing the compatibility of the cup product with products of internal Homs, analogous to (3.7.8.1); Traces and cup products of perfect filtered complexes, Proposition 2.7 (2), proves the formula (3.8.8) on morphisms.

V 4.4.4, 4.4.5, 4.4.6, 4.5.2, 4.5.3 for objects of D^-F(A) (resp. D^-G(A)) not concentrated in degrees <= 0: the diagonal maps phi^n: LS^n(L (x)^L M) -> LS^n L (x)^L LS^n M and psi^n, and their compatibilities, are constructed in Diagonal maps of symmetric and exterior powers for connective L, M only (Remark 2.5 there). The general case needs a natural isomorphism Tot N S^n(Gamma iP (x) Gamma iQ) = LS^n(P (x) Q) in D(A) for bounded above flat P, Q (the mixed object of a tensor product against the termwise tensor product of mixed objects), not proved in the course; numerical evidence in plan/cotangent_complex_20261020/C2_PLAN.md.

V (5.2.1), (5.2.4), 5.3.1, 5.3.2 for coefficient objects M not concentrated in degrees <= 0, and V 5.3.3 for E not concentrated in degrees <= 0: L-series of endomorphisms of perfect complexes defines L_t(f) for M in D^{<=0}(A) (any E of bounded perfect amplitude, through even shifts, Definition 3.5 there) and proves the exterior-power formula for E, M in D^{<=0}(A) (Corollary 3.7 there). The general case needs the diagonal maps phi^n, psi^n for non-connective objects (the obligation for V 4.4.4-4.5.3).

V Remark 5.5.3 with the integral rank rg: K^0(B) -> H^0(T, Z) of perfect complexes over a local ring (SGA 6): Chern classes of perfect complexes, Corollary 1.4, proves that c_t and the trace of the identity are additive on triangles; the integral rank is not constructed in the course.

V 5.9 (last paragraph) and V 6.2 for morphisms of complex analytic spaces: Chern classes with supports from partial connections proves the construction of V §6 for every derivation d: B -> Omega into a locally free module of finite rank, with the principal parts B (+) Omega of d (Lemma 2.2), and Chern classes of perfect complexes treats the module of differentials Omega_{B/A}. The analytic theory needs the identification of the analytic principal parts and analytic differentials (Grothendieck, Techniques de construction en géométrie analytique VII, Séminaire Henri Cartan 13 (1960/61), exposé 14, https://www.numdam.org/item/SHC_1960-1961__13_2_A1_0/) with the principal parts of the analytic differential; this identification is not proved in the course.

III 3.3.2, footnote: the isomorphism H_1(L_{B/A}) = Tor^A_1(B, B) = I/I^2 obtained from the augmentation ideal of the Tor resolution (The fundamental spectral sequence, Proposition 1.1 (3)) coincides with the isomorphism H^{-1}(L_{B/A}) = I/I^2 of the theory of infinitesimal extensions (II 1.2.8.1; in the course, through the naive cotangent complex, Theorem 6.1 of The cotangent complex). Both are natural isomorphisms of I/I^2, so they differ by a sign fixed on the universal example Z[t] -> Z; the comparison is not proved in the course, and no statement of the course depends on it.

III 3.3.7 for an arbitrary ringed topos, with Illusie's base change theorem II 2.2.3: for a Tor-independent cocartesian square of rings of a topos, L_{B/A} (x)^L_B B' -> L_{B'/A'} is an isomorphism, so weak complete intersections are stable under such base change. Weak complete intersections proves it for topoi with enough points, through stalks (Proposition 5.1), and for schemes (Corollary 5.2). The general case needs the independence of the cotangent complex of the free simplicial resolution in a topos; not proved in the course.

Weak complete intersections, Lemma 4.1: the value of the universal sign lambda in c = lambda d, where c is the connecting map of the transitivity triangle of A -> P -> P/I on H^{-1}, read through the conormal isomorphism of The fundamental spectral sequence, Proposition 1.1 (3). No statement of the course depends on it; its value is tied to the footnote of III 3.3.2 recorded above. Not determined in the course.

Deforming a morphism together with its target, Section 5: the second argument of III 2.3.5 is not given. With a flat deformation Y of Y_o over Z chosen, the obstruction o(Y) to extending f_o to a morphism X -> Y over Z lies in Ext^1(Lf_o^* L_{Y_o/Z_o}, h_o^* K) (III 2.2.4; for ringed topoi this is Stacks Tag 08UG, with the naive cotangent complex, whose Ext^1 agrees); to be proved: o(Y') - o(Y) is the image of the difference u in Ext^1(L_{Y_o/Z_o}, g_o^* K) of the classes of Y' and Y, and the connecting map carries o(Y) to the obstruction omega of Theorem 3.2. Home: an added proposition in that lesson, after Proposition 5.1.

Formal categories with divided powers and the Čech–Alexander complex, Sections 1-2: Illusie defines divided power structures, PD formal categories and PD-adic ones (VIII 1.2.3, 1.2.4) for arbitrary K-formal categories (internal categories of the opposite of pro-K-algebras). The lesson treats strict formal categories (projective systems of affine categories), which include all envelopes and completions used later. To be settled: either every K-formal category is isomorphic to a strict one, or Definition 2.5 and Propositions 2.6-2.7 hold for non-strict ones with divided powers on pro-ideals. Home: an added proposition in that lesson, after Definition 1.3.

The de Rham complex of a formal category with divided powers, Section 3: VIII 1.2.10 b) states that for a group scheme G over S, omega^bullet_{G/S} is the de Rham complex (Proposition 3.4) of the G-invariant direct image on S of the Čech–Alexander complex of G/S, and an analogous statement for a torsor X -> Y (VIII 1.1.3 c)). Not proved: build the invariant direct image of the Čech–Alexander complex as a PD formal category over S (resp. Y), identify its Omega^1 with omega^1 (De Rham complexes and Lie algebroids, Proposition 6.3), check which case of Proposition 3.4 applies (d^0 = d^1 when Y = S) and compare the differentials. Home: an added example in that lesson, after Example 3.5.

Décalage and the formal Poincaré lemma: VIII 1.3.6 states that, for a fixed K-algebra A, the functor R -> Omega^bullet_R is an equivalence between PD-adic K-formal categories with object A and flat module of differentials and de Rham complexes over A/K with flat degree 1 term, that every such R is a groupoid whose inversion acts by (-1)^n on Omega^n, and (with De Rham complexes and Lie algebroids, Theorem 5.3) that it contains Cartier's equivalence of formal groups and Lie algebras in characteristic 0. Illusie attributes the construction to Quillen (rebuild P^n inductively as the fibre product of Remark 3.4) and gives no proof. Home: a following lesson of Part F, after Remark 3.4.

Décalage and the formal Poincaré lemma: VIII 1.3.4.4 a) states that for a smooth X -> S and R the Čech–Alexander complex of X/S, Omega^bullet of the shifted category is the linearization of Omega^bullet_{X/S} in the sense of Grothendieck's 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' 2.2, so that Corollary 3.1 (3) gives the formal Poincaré lemma 3.2 there. The lesson proves the polynomial case (Example 3.3); the comparison with the linearization for smooth X/S is not written. Home: a remark in that lesson, after Example 3.3.

Localization morphisms and the cotangent complex: Illusie II 2.3.4 states that for the spectrum X~ of a ringed topos X in the sense of Hakim, with projection p, the map p^{-1}O_X -> O_X~ is a localization morphism; II 2.3.8 and 2.3.9 state that for relative schemes over a ringed topos in the sense of Hakim, the structure ring of a base change X' (resp. of a fibre product Z) is a localization of u^{-1}O_X (x) f'^{-1}O_S' (resp. of p^{-1}O_X (x) q^{-1}O_Y). Hakim's spectrum and relative schemes are not constructed in the course. Given these statements, II 2.3.5 is Corollary 2.4 of the lesson and II 2.3.10-2.3.11 are Theorem 4.2 and Corollary 4.3; for ordinary schemes the localization property is Proposition 4.4. Home: a lesson on the spectrum of a ringed topos and relative schemes, after this one.

Derived de Rham complexes in characteristic p: Illusie VIII 2.1.4.3 states a canonical functorial isomorphism C^{-1}: (+)_i Lambda^i L_{B^(p)/A}[-i] -> L Omega_{B/A} in D(A). The lesson proves the statement on the graded pieces of the conjugate filtration (Theorem 3.2); the argument given for the decomposition uses a Cartier map into Omega that does not exist (Remark 1.2). Bhatt (arXiv 1204.6560, Section 3; Illusie's erratum) states that the decomposition fails as a B^(1)-linear splitting for a singularity not liftable to Z/p^2, for instance B = F_p[x_1,...,x_6]/(x_i^p, x_1x_2 + x_3x_4 + x_5x_6) (Berthelot-Ogus), the first extension of the conjugate filtration being the obstruction to lifting B^(1). Not written: the identification of that extension with the lifting obstruction (through Deligne-Illusie) and the non-liftability of the example. Home: a remark in this lesson.

Derived de Rham complexes in characteristic p: Bhatt's liftable Cartier isomorphism (arXiv 1204.6560, Section 3): for a map of flat Z/p^2-algebras with compatible lifts of Frobenius, the conjugate filtration of the derived de Rham complex of the reductions mod p splits, as algebras. Not written; the published proof uses Quillen's model structure on simplicial algebras over Z/p^2. Home: a section of this lesson or of Part G.

The completed derived de Rham complex of a complete intersection: Illusie VIII 2.2.4 (ii), 2.2.5 and 2.2.6 in their second case (T punctual, A noetherian, Q smooth over A, I regular, any characteristic). The missing input is Berthelot's lemma: for a regular ideal the graded ring of the divided power envelope, for the divided power filtration, is the divided power algebra of I/I^2; with it, the proofs of Corollary 3.2 and Theorem 4.1 apply to the PD-adically completed Čech–Alexander complexes. Not written. Home: a section of this lesson.

The completed derived de Rham complex of a complete intersection: Illusie VIII 2.2.7-2.2.8: for a complete intersection morphism f: X -> S, smoothable if S has characteristic 0, or with S affine noetherian and X affine, Rf_cris*(O^_X/S) = Rf_*(L Omega^_X/S) in the completed filtered derived category, for the PD-nilpotent crystalline topos. Not written: that topos and the computation of its cohomology by completed Čech–Alexander complexes of a smoothing; the algebraic comparison is Theorem 4.1 with Remark 4.2 in characteristic 0. Home: a lesson on crystalline cohomology after this one.

The completed derived de Rham complex of a complete intersection: Illusie VIII 2.2.1 for an arbitrary affine A-category C with a surjection C -> B whose degree 0 kernel I is weakly regular and U/U^2 flat; the lesson proves it for the Čech nerve (Lemma 2.2, Proposition 2.3), which is the case used. The general case needs the divided power envelope of the nerve in place of the nerve. Home: a remark in this lesson.
